key_insight: Replace passive, global fusion of 3D geometry with an active perception paradigm that selectively queries and aligns geometric priors to semantic tokens, reducing redundancy and semantic-geometry misalignment to improve spatial reasoning.
problem_solved: Current MLLM integrations treat geometry as a single global stream, causing noisy or misaligned geometric signals that hurt spatial understanding and produce redundant features.
method: Active Geometry Integration module: the model issues targeted queries to a 3D encoder to extract region- or token-specific geometric cues instead of ingesting a single global feature.
Selective alignment & fusion: geometry features are matched to semantic/visual tokens with attention or gating so only relevant geometric information is incorporated.
Sparse, interpretable fusion pipeline: explicit geometry-aware reasoning steps reduce redundancy, improve efficiency, and make the geometry–semantics mapping more transparent.
impact: Enables more accurate, efficient, and interpretable spatial reasoning in multimodal models, benefiting tasks like visual question answering, embodied navigation, and robot perception where precise geometry–semantic alignment matters.

Bar chart or table: performance and efficiency gains (accuracy on spatial tasks, reduced redundant features/compute)
paper_title: Thinking with Geometry: Active Geometry Integration for Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Tao Tang, Kun Xiang, Zihan Guo
